item.title: Google DeepMind melds humans and AI agents to vet Signal's secure messaging techniques
item.description: Google DeepMind researchers have completed a formal verification of Signal's messaging security, marking what they claim is the first time AI has helped devise a proof that links protocol-level security guarantees to a widely used cryptographic implementation. They did so using AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent framework for formal software specification and verification. AlphaProof Code relies on a human-guided agent that writes a Lean specification, assesses machine code semantics, and crafts an agent-authored proof that the Lean kernel checks against the specification. In this instance, AlphaProof Code verified Signal’s post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet , thereby validating the design of libsignal 's forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security, and handshake secrecy. In so doing, the Google/DeepMind team – Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger, Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, Charles Sutton, and Pushmeet Kohli – has taken a step toward a challenge the Beneficial AI Foundation issued in April to formally verify the Signal protocol and Signal app with Lean. The AlphaProof Code process involves working with various models to turn Signal's security goals into a human-reviewed mathematical specification. Based on this spec, the researchers assigned Gemini Carbon agents to generate Lean code proving the correctness of the libsignal implementation. After the agents generated 6.5 million lines of Lean code, they undertook an auditing pass and flagged bits that required human review. The result is theoretical in that it assumes perfect cryptography and doesn't guarantee the computational secrecy of bytes. But it's still a meaningful assertion of correctness. "It's a system that is fundamentally built for human AI collaboration," said Swarat Chaudhuri, research scientist at Google DeepMind and a professor at the University of Texas at Austin, in an interview with The Register . Traditionally, said Chaudhuri, you start proving theorems with well-defined problems formulated by a mathematician that get submitted to an AI agent for proof. In this case, the researchers had to figure out what to prove. "In formal methods, we always had this belief that verification is the hard bit," he said. "There's thirty or forty years of work on how to scale up verification. Now we are able to do that. So now the question is what are we verifying? … That process is fundamentally human-in-the-loop, but we devised a process of trying to scale it up to the extent possible with AI." As Chaudhuri and his colleagues note in their research paper, "AlphaProof Code: Verifying Signal’s Security at the Machine-Code Level," formal verification used to require heroic efforts. Formally verifying the seL4 microkernel took 20 person-years, while developing the verified CompCert C compiler took six years. item.title: Gombe records 98 road crash deaths, 1,345 injuries in nine months — FRSC
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe GOMBE — The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has disclosed that 98 persons were killed while 1,345 others sustained injuries in road traffic crashes recorded across Gombe State between January and September 2026. The FRSC Sector Commander in the state, Commander Samson Kaura, disclosed this on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing members of the Gombe State Council of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) during the commemoration of the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. Kaura said the command recorded 1,345 road traffic incidents during the nine-month period, adding that fatalities increased by six per cent compared with the corresponding period. He identified excessive speeding and reckless driving as major causes of road crashes and fatalities, warning that irresponsible road use continued to pose a serious threat to motorists and other road users. According to him, the annual World Day of Remembrance provides an opportunity to honour those who have lost their lives or sustained serious injuries in road crashes, while drawing attention to the need for stronger legal responses to traffic offences resulting in deaths and injuries. He said the commemoration also seeks to promote better support for crash victims and their families, as well as evidence-based interventions to prevent and ultimately eliminate road traffic deaths and injuries. The sector commander expressed concern that the fatalities recorded in the first nine months of 2026 had surpassed the figure for the whole of 2025. He said the command recorded 1,614 road traffic incidents in 2025, resulting in 92 deaths and 926 injuries. Kaura described the 2026 World Day of Remembrance as a campaign aimed at translating remembrance into concrete action, stressing the need for collective responsibility in addressing road traffic crashes. In his response, the Vice Chairman of the Gombe State NUJ Council, Emmanuel Akila, who represented the state chairman, Faruk Muazu Gombe, pledged the union’s continued cooperation with the FRSC in promoting road safety and development. Akila, however, urged the FRSC to strengthen collaboration with the union to identify and curb the activities of fake journalists in the state. He called on the corps to insist on proper identification of journalists during official engagements and other road-related activities to prevent impersonation and protect the integrity of the journalism profession. The NUJ vice chairman also urged the FRSC to intensify enforcement against vehicle overloading, describing the practice as one of the factors contributing to fatalities in road crashes. He stressed the need for sustained public enlightenment, effective enforcement of traffic regulations and stronger collaboration among relevant stakeholders to reduce road crashes and safeguard lives on the highways. The post Gombe records 98 road crash deaths, 1,345 injuries in nine months — FRSC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ranking top 3 Steelers most likely to be dealt at 2026 NFL trade deadline
item.description: Ranking top 3 Steelers most likely to be dealt at 2026 NFL trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Pittsburgh Steelers have rediscovered their winning formula. However, that does not mean every player on their roster is untouchable. Sitting at 6-2 and leading the AFC North, Mike McCarthy’s team has legitimate postseason ambitions. Still, general manager Omar Khan must consider whether certain roster pieces could be more valuable as trade assets than as depth options. With the November 10 deadline approaching, Pittsburgh has a chance to address its remaining weaknesses. QB Mason Rudolph Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images The most logical trade candidate is veteran quarterback Mason Rudolph . Pittsburgh’s decision to carry four quarterbacks on its initial 53-man roster was an unusual luxury. Of course, Aaron Rodgers firmly established as the starter. Will Howard and Drew Allar represent developmental options. Rudolph, meanwhile, is a veteran with extensive starting experience. He could provide immediate stability to a team suddenly dealing with a quarterback crisis. At 31, Rudolph has appeared in 37 career games and made 19 starts. He also knows Pittsburgh’s system and has demonstrated that he can operate an NFL offense when called upon. His two-year, $7.5 million contract is relatively affordable. That makes him a potentially attractive option for a contender seeking a reliable backup or temporary starter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) There is already a plausible market for experienced quarterbacks. Minnesota, for instance, could explore additional depth after moving on from JJ McCarthy. Injuries elsewhere could also create another opening. However, Pittsburgh should not assume that Rudolph will command a premium selection. He has made only one start since returning to the Steelers in 2025. A conditional late-round pick may be a more realistic return. Still, moving him would create roster flexibility. That could potentially give Khan another asset to address offensive tackle or secondary depth. CB Asante Samuel Jr. Asante Samuel Jr. ranks second, although trading him would be considerably more complicated. The cornerback signed a one-year, $4 million contract with Pittsburgh in March. That makes him a potential free agent after the season. It also gives the Steelers a reason to consider extracting value now. Samuel has also played enough meaningful football to attract interest. He has started all eight games in 2026. He has recorded 28 tackles and eight passes defended. His experience and ability to contribute in different coverage looks could appeal to teams looking for another dependable defensive back. At 27, he is also young enough to offer more than a short-term rental. However, Pittsburgh should be careful about creating a hole it cannot easily fill. item.title: Champions Classic history: Duke, Kansas, Kentucky and Michigan State bring legendary records to Chicago
item.description: Champions Classic history: Duke, Kansas, Kentucky and Michigan State bring legendary records to Chicago originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Champions Classic returns Tuesday with another doubleheader featuring four of college basketball's most recognizable programs. Michigan State faces Duke in the opening game at Chicago's United Center, followed by Kansas against Kentucky. The event began in 2011 and has become one of the sport's premier early-season showcases, bringing nationally prominent teams together before conference play begins. Over the years, the Champions Classic has produced remarkable performances, memorable victories and several moments that helped define entire college basketball seasons. Duke's 2018 victory remains unforgettable One of the event's most famous games came in 2018, when Duke overwhelmed Kentucky 118-84. Champions Classic Standings heading into tomorrow https://t.co/hHR3Xxbz3w — Steven Peake (@StevenPeakeKSR) November 10, 2026 The Blue Devils featured an extraordinary freshman class led by Zion Williamson, RJ Barrett and Cam Reddish. Duke's 118 points established a Champions Classic scoring record, while the 34-point victory remains the event's largest winning margin. The performance immediately established Duke as one of the most discussed teams in the country and provided a national introduction to its highly anticipated freshman stars. Michigan State produced the event's overtime classic The 2022 Champions Classic featured a memorable contest between Michigan State and Kentucky. The Spartans defeated the Wildcats in double overtime, producing the event's only overtime game through its first 15 editions. The result demonstrated why the Champions Classic has become such an appealing event. Although the games take place early in the season, the quality of the participants can create an atmosphere resembling a major postseason contest. Chicago has become an important home Tuesday marks the fifth time Chicago has hosted the Champions Classic. The United Center previously welcomed the event in 2013, 2015, 2017 and 2023, tying Madison Square Garden for the most hosting appearances. The doubleheader also continues a tradition involving the same four programs since the event's creation. Duke, Kansas, Kentucky and Michigan State have collectively produced numerous national championships and generations of recognizable college basketball stars. MORE : Champions Classic history: Greatest moments before Duke, Kansas, Kentucky and Michigan State meet again Another chapter begins Tuesday Michigan State and Duke meet at 7 p.m. ET, while Kansas and Kentucky follow at 9:30 p.m. ET. The games provide early opportunities to evaluate teams with substantial expectations and passionate national followings. item.title: Jockey Neale, 22, dies after fall during race
item.description: Izzy Neale turned professional in 2024 and rode 88 winners in her professional career [Getty Images] Jockey Izzy Neale has died after falling from her horse during a race at Warren Racecourse in Australia on Sunday. The 22-year-old was dislodged from her horse Marnoo and was airlifted to Dubbo hospital. Neale's family announced on Tuesday that she had passed away from her injuries. "It is with deep sadness and broken hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved Izzy, surrounded by her closest family and friends," a joint statement from the family and Racing NSW said. "Izzy rode horses before she could walk. Her love of horses was a lifelong passion that, more recently, had grown into a love of racing. "Through organ donation, Izzy will give others the chance of life, bringing some comfort to our family amid this devastating loss. "We are deeply grateful for the love, kindness and support shown to Izzy and our family by her friends, the racing community and everyone who has been by our side during this heartbreaking time." The rest of the Cotton Cup meeting was abandoned and Neale's horse Marnoo was euthanised after sustaining a serious leg injury in the accident. A second rider, Diego Montes de Oca, was injured in the same race. He suffered minor injuries to his foot and has since been discharged from hospital. Neale was an apprentice rider and rode 88 winners in her professional career. The Australian Turf club described Neale as a "talented young rider with a bright future". Trainer John Thompson, who Neale worked for, also paid tribute. "An absolute beacon of shining light. Always happy. Always smiling. Loved by everyone who met her," he said on X. "The world is poorer for the loss of a beautiful young lady. Heartbreaking." Neale's family thanked the public and the racing authorities in Australia for their support, as well as the medical staff who cared for her. "As we come to terms with our loss, we ask that our family's privacy be respected," they said. "Izzy was dearly loved and will forever be in our hearts." Latest horse racing results

item.title: Wales call up MK Dons' Collins as Moore withdraws
item.description: Aaron Collins (right) has seven goals in the past three games for MK Dons and is the EFL's joint-top goalscorer [Getty Images] Wales have called up uncapped MK Dons striker Aaron Collins for this month's Nations League matches following Wrexham frontman Kieffer Moore's withdrawal due to injury. Moore, 34, left the field during Wrexham's 1-1 Championship draw with Wolves on Saturday. Wales have not specified what kind of injury the 57-cap forward has sustained. He is replaced in the Wales squad by Collins, who has scored 17 goals in 16 games across all competitions for League One side Dons this season, including four goals in a game against Doncaster last month. The 29-year-old former Newport County player joins Craig Bellamy's squad for concluding Group A4 games in Norway and at home to Portugal. Newport-born Collins has played for 10 different - mainly lower league - clubs since leaving Rodney Parade for Wolverhampton Wanderers in 2016. Wales, who are looking to preserve their place in the Nations League's top tier, face Norway in Oslo on Saturday before finishing their campaign at home against Portugal next Tuesday. Wales are third in Group A4, with their only win from four matches so far coming against World Cup quarter-finalists Norway in Cardiff last month. Bellamy is without midfielder Jordan James but has influential Leeds pair Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon back, along with Cardiff playmaker Rubin Colwill. Bellamy's side could still finish in second, third or fourth place. A top-two spot would take Wales to the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027. Finishing third would mean a relegation play-off against a League B team in March, while finishing bottom of the group would result in either a relegation play-off or direct relegation, depending on the ranking with other League A groups. item.title: Rudi Völler suggests Thomas Müller could follow him into DFB role
item.description: Rudi Völler suggests Thomas Müller could follow him into DFB role Rudi Völler has named former Bayern Munich star Thomas Müller as a potential successor to him as sporting director of the German Football Association (DFB). The 66-year-old, whose current deal expires in 2028, said on the “Kerners 11” podcast: “At some point, my time will finally come to an end. And if the DFB – whether [DFB president] Bernd Neuendorf, [DFB vice-president] Aki Watzke or managing director Per Mertesacker – feels that someone else should be brought in, I think that would be a good idea.” Völler added that he's "absolutely convinced" Müller would be suitable for the role. "Thomas could certainly do it, just like others could. Whether in my position or another one. They would just have to want it – that's the basis," he said. Since leaving Bayern Munich at the end of the 2024/25 season, 36-year-old Müller has been playing for Vancouver Whitecaps in Major League Soccer, where his contract runs until the summer of 2027.

item.title: NFL trade deadline grades: Live analysis for Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates, and more 2026 deadline deals
item.description: NFL trade deadline grades: Live analysis for Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates, and more 2026 deadline deals originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There used to be crickets around the NFL's midseason trade deadline. That has been replaced by a swarm of cicadas, with teams buzzing about making plenty of deals, big and small. In 2024, the league saw 13 in-season trades. Last year, that number skyrocketed to 22 such trades, with 27 players changing teams. This year, going back to the Giants getting J.J. McCarthy from the Vikings , seven trades were executed before November. Five more have already gone down this month. With the 2026 deadline here on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET, there is still the expected big splash of a three-time Pro Bowl running back leaving a hard-fading AFC team to a strong contending NFC team. Although Indianapolis has already been busy selling, several other teams, led by Jacksonville, got focused on buying. Here is a breakdown of all the deals, going back to mid-October. LIVE: Follow latest NFL trade rumors, updates NFL trade deadline grades Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Jaguars trade for Eagles DT Jordan Davis Grade: B The Jaguars completed their strong defensive line with Davis joining Arik Armstead in the middle between Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen. Davis adds a needed extra inside disruptor to join the big-play mentality of coordinator Anthony Campanile. Jacksonville is definitely trying to load up with a championship-level defense. MORE: Inside Eagles' draft pick stash Jaguars trade for Falcons S Jessie Bates III Grade: A+ The Jaguars were fully expected to get a safety after Eric Murray (elbow) went down for the season, with rumors swirling most around Derwin James and Budda Baker. Once Bates was available from Atlanta, however, he had to be the move to pair him with Antonio Johnson. Bates is a flat-out playmaker and joins an Anthony Campanile defense built on getting takeaways. This is a huge impact at a position of need for a true Super Bowl contender. MORE: Jaguars' updated defensive depth chart Ravens trade for Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett Grade: B Baltimore needed to do something to be respectable at quarterback for the sake of the offense. The timing of Brissett's benching in Arizona was ideal. Brissett will at least facilitate a legitimate passing game with Baltimore's weapons. Reunited with his former Cardinals QB coach Israel Woolfork, Brissett can quickly learn the offense ahead of a winnable home Monday game against the Chargers . Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Bears trade for Titans DT Jeffery Simmons Grade: A Simmons was a literal massive splurge by Chicago, but they got the same outstanding, dominant force he was in Tennessee. He made an immediate impact, getting his first sack for his new team in Week 9 as his front crushed the Seahawks . item.title: Liverpool leading the race to sign Bundesliga defender
item.description: Liverpool leading the race to sign Bundesliga defender Liverpool Lead Castello Lukeba Race as Defensive Planning Accelerates Liverpool’s transfer window continues to move on several fronts, and one of the more persuasive developments concerns Castello Lukeba. According to Football FanCast, the Merseyside club are currently the most interested Premier League side in signing the RB Leipzig centre-back, with Arsenal and Manchester United also in the picture. What gives this report added weight is the suggestion that the player’s camp have made clear his preference for a move to the Premier League. That does not make a deal imminent, and it certainly does not remove the complexity of negotiating with Leipzig, but it does shape the landscape. When a player’s representatives begin informing interested clubs of a desired destination, recruitment departments tend to sharpen their focus quickly. Photo: IMAGO Castello Lukeba emerges in Liverpool transfer plans Liverpool have already committed huge money to squad building, yet the sense remains that defensive work is still ongoing. That is understandable. Squad planning rarely stops at headline spending totals, particularly when contract timelines and age profiles begin to influence medium-term decisions. At centre-back, there is an obvious need to think ahead. Virgil van Dijk remains a towering presence, but any elite club must prepare for succession before necessity becomes urgency. Joe Gomez’s situation also forms part of that wider conversation, while depth across the back line has been examined closely as Andoni Iraola shapes the next phase of his squad. Lukeba, at 23, fits the profile Liverpool often pursue when they believe a player can grow into a leading role. He is young, already experienced at a high level, and naturally left-footed, an attribute that can materially influence build-up structure and balance in a back line. Those qualities alone help explain why multiple English clubs have tracked him. RB Leipzig defender suits Andoni Iraola system The tactical appeal is clear. Liverpool’s defensive unit needs players comfortable defending space, aggressive in duels and composed enough to progress possession under pressure. Lukeba has long been regarded as a defender with those traits, which is why admiration around Europe has endured. Another point in this case is contractual. The original report indicates that Lukeba has a release clause, which can simplify parts of a transfer if a buying club decide conditions are favourable. A clause does not guarantee completion, but it can offer certainty over the level required to open the door. That matters in a market where Liverpool are balancing ambition with discipline. They have spent heavily, but that does not mean they will abandon structure. Any significant move from here is likely to be driven by conviction rather than noise. item.title: ‘Scariest part’: Dwyane Wade says Steph Curry’s ‘best skill’ is not actually his shooting
item.description: Photo by Tom Pennington/Getty Images Steph Curry is one of the best players in the world. The Golden State Warriors superstar is still playing at an elite level at the age of 38, and he is continuing to break all sorts of records. Most people would say that Curry’s best skill is his shooting from three-point range, but Dwyane Wade thinks it’s actually something else. Dwyane Wade says Steph Curry’s cardio is actually his best skill Curry is widely regarded as the greatest shooter in basketball history. The way he shoots and the areas he occupies completely changed how defences guard the perimeter, and he’s still impossible to stop at times. That is why many would call shooting Curry’s best skill, but Wade believes it’s his cardio and off-ball movement. He said on his podcast : “I think his best skill is his cardiovascular. Steph doesn’t look like he ever gets tired. He’s always moving. “The scariest part about guarding Steph Curry is when he gives the ball up. That’s saying a lot about a guy who was dynamic with the ball in his hand. But when Steph Curry gives that ball up, watch out! “That’s what makes them (Warriors) great is when Steph gives that ball up and now he is moving, and everybody is doing their job. They’re setting screens in. They’re ducking in. “You had guys that wanted to be isolation guys. They don’t do a lot of isolation basketball in Golden State. It’s movement. It’s body movement. It’s ball movement. It’s making sure that the defence is not comfortable in their positions.” Wade finished off by saying that Curry’s mere presence on the court is an assist to everyone else because of his movement with and without the ball. “Forget hockey assist. Steph on the floor is an assist for everybody because of his body movement and the ball movement that comes with that.” We’d still attribute Curry’s best skill to shooting, but Wade’s assessment makes complete sense. The way the 38-year-old moves with and without the ball makes him so difficult to guard. All it takes is one mistake, and that opens the door for him to shoot – and he almost always scores. That is why Curry is among the greatest players of all time. item.title: UK, Nigeria seal $750m infrastructure deal as Pension funds prepare to unlock billions
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Nigeria and the United Kingdom have strengthened their economic partnership with a proposed $750 million infrastructure investment fund aimed at mobilising billions of dollars in pension assets to finance critical development projects across Nigeria and other selected African markets. The initiative, which has already attracted interest from 19 Nigerian pension funds, is expected to channel long-term domestic and international investments into key sectors, including energy, transportation and digital infrastructure, as both countries seek to address the continent’s widening infrastructure financing gap. A statement from PenCom disclosed that the agreement was signed by Nigeria’s Pension Industry Leadership Council, PILC,and UK-funded specialist development agency, FSD Africa, in Lagos on November 10, 2026. Under the agreement, FSD Africa will provide technical expertise and advisory support to PILC towards establishing the proposed investment platform, including the selection of a fund manager through a competitive process, engagement with prospective investors and development finance institutions, capacity building and support for necessary regulatory reforms. The initiative was developed by Nigerian Pension Fund Administrators, PFAs, with support from the National Pension Commission, PenCom, and FSD Africa. Speaking on the development, UK Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Jonny Baxter, said the partnership reflected the shared commitment of both countries to mobilising domestic capital, particularly pension funds, for productive investment in the real economy. According to him: “The UK is proud to partner with the Nigeria’s Pension Industry and the pensions regulator Pencom to progress this investment. Both our countries are prioritising tacking the challenge of attracting more domestic capital, including from pension funds, into the real economy. It is great to see Nigeria making concrete progress on its efforts and be a part of those opportunities to turn this ambition into investment, jobs, and economic growth.” On her part, Chair of the Nigeria Pension Industry Leadership Council and Director-General of the National Pension Commission, Ms Omolola Oloworaran, described the proposed investment platform as timely, stressing that the pension industry was committed to deploying its substantial pool of long-term savings towards national development while protecting contributors’ retirement funds. She said: “The pension industry holds the largest pool of long-term savings capital in the country, and we are committed to mobilising it to deepen infrastructure development, while safeguarding the retirement savings of contributors. This MoU is the first step we are taking as an industry, and it is just the beginning.” In the same vein, Chief Executive Officer of FSD Africa, Mark Napier, said the initiative would help address the contradiction between Africa’s substantial institutional capital and its huge infrastructure financi

item.title: Amber Glenn out of Grand Prix Series while competing on 'Dancing with the Stars'
item.description: Amber Glenn withdrew from both of her fall Grand Prix Series figure skating events while she competes on "Dancing with the Stars." Glenn, a three-time U.S. champion who was fifth in her Olympic debut, was crossed out of the entry list Tuesday for NHK Trophy in Japan, which is two weeks from now, the last event of the six-event Grand Prix regular season. Glenn previously withdrew from Saatva Skate America, which is this week in Everett, Washington. 2026 Saatva Skate America: How to watch, schedule, preview of figure skating Grand Prix Skate America, the biggest annual international figure skating event in the U.S., airs live on NBC Sports and Peacock. Nick Zaccardi , The world's top skaters can each compete twice over the Grand Prix regular season, with the top six per discipline qualifying for December's Grand Prix Final, the second-biggest event this season behind March's World Championships. In 2024, Glenn won the Grand Prix Final, which at the time was the most prestigious international title for a U.S. women's singles skater in 14 years. Glenn has not ruled out competing later this season, including at the Prevagen U.S. Championships in January. Her current streak of three national titles is the longest for a women's singles skater since Michelle Kwan won all eight from 1998-2005. Alysa Liu, the 2026 Olympic gold medalist and 2025 World champion, previously announced she is taking this season off. Isabeau Levito, the 2024 World silver medalist who was 12th in her Olympic debut, is the top returning U.S. woman competing on the Grand Prix. She was third at Skate Canada in October and is entered in next week's Grand Prix Finland. item.title: “Aaron Judge Is Going To Have Big Man Injuries Like Giancarlo Stanton” – MLB Insider Questions Fit of Corey Seager in Potential Yankees Trade
item.description: Corey Seager | © Instagram/ @rangers MLB insider Joel Sherman gave a blunt assessment of whether Rangers star Corey Seager could solve the Yankees’ hitting woes. His comments came in response to fellow insider Jon Heyman’s column, which suggested Seager could fit into the Yankees’ lineup. Sherman agreed the Bronx Bombers need a bat but, unlike Heyman, didn’t name a specific player. He urged caution about Seager’s offense, citing his strikeouts and limited playing time. He said relying on Giancarlo Stanton’s bat would be silly and warned against overreading captain Aaron Judge’s slump, as age may increase his injury risk. “He struck out almost 24 percent of the time last year, Seager, which was by far the most. It just feels like you’re going to buy the last five injury-prone years… I personally don’t love the name because I think he’s trending in all the wrong ways, both in performance and health,” Sherman said via The Show podcast. I can’t count on Stanton at all, and probably a little less on Judge just staying healthy now at 35 in his mid-30s. He’s going to have big-man injuries like Stanton… I think they need another bat… I keep scouring, looking for the name. I can’t find it, except to tell you I’d be really afraid of the last five years of Seager’s contract,” he added. Watch the video here: Multiple injuries and IL stints severely limited Seager’s playing time in 2026. Last month, he underwent successful arthroscopic surgery to remove a bone spur from his right elbow and is expected to recover fully and be ready for spring training next year. Seager signed a massive 10-year, $325 million contract with the Rangers before the 2022 season and helped the team win its first World Series title in 2023, earning World Series MVP honors. The five-time All-Star has five years remaining on his contract, which runs through 2031. item.title: What LA Rams sources were saying about Terrance Ferguson just before his hamstring injury
item.description: Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images Terrance Ferguson has played just three games so far this season for the Los Angeles Rams, so here’s the latest from sources within the camp. The Los Angeles Rams are 5-4 through nine games this season, with their most recent game a 13-20 loss to the Commanders just as they were gaining momentum. It’s clear they are missing sophomore tight end Terrance Ferguson, who has missed six games due to a variety of issues. Just as he was coming back from an ankle issue, Ferguson did his hamstring, and it threw a spanner in the works for the Rams. LA Rams sources on Terrance Ferguson The Rams intended to slowly bring Ferguson along after he played 14 games last season and started only three of those. The three games he did play this season were all starts, so the Rams clearly have a bigger role for him this season, even though he hasn’t been able to fulfil it. The Rams could certainly use his explosiveness, but repeated injuries to the lower half of his body will eventually take a toll on his output. Meanwhile, his hamstring injury set him back further, and according to Graziano, speaking on ESPN, it is a huge blow because Ferguson figured to be a huge part of their plans this season. He said: “I was talking to Rams people on Friday, just doing prep for the game, and a couple of people were talking about how with Davante out, it’s just Puka. How do you combat that? “They said, “Well, we’re like the 13 personnel team.” Obviously, they’ve got the tight ends. They were saying having Terrance Ferguson back this week is massive. He’s a huge part of the game plan. “This was Friday at 5 p.m. Eastern. Ten minutes after those phone calls were over, I got the updated Rams injury report. Terrance Ferguson had pulled his hamstring in practice. He’s not going to play. So they had a Terrance Ferguson game plan.” Knowing what we know now, it’s not very surprising that the Rams lost to the Commanders, since a huge part of their plans pulled out of the game on short notice before the game. Now the wait begins on his latest injury, hoping that the layoff is not huge, but he looks like a certainty to miss their next game against the Cardinals. At least they will know they are planning without him this time! item.title: No Suspension for Tom Wilson after Hit on Sandis Vilmanis. That’s Wrong
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Washington Capitals play in Ottawa tonight and Tom Wilson will be in the lineup as if his cheap hit on Florida rookie Sandis Vilmanis never happened. Perhaps we did not see it as well as the NHL’s Department of Player Safety did. Wilson, long one of the NHL’s biggest cheap-shot artists, will not face any sort of supplemental discipline for boarding Vilmanis in the first period of Washington’s 4-3 win over the Panthers on Saturday afternoon. The punishment, we guess, of being kicked out of the game was plenty enough. Wilson has probably learned his lesson. After being suspended six other times, we seriously doubt it. And, based on the language Wilson used on the game officials who tossed him Saturday as he took his sweet time getting to the Washington room, he thought that punishment was too harsh. Really, it was not even close to being enough. Florida coach Paul Maurice was asked about the hit and deferred comment, saying he would “save that for the Department of Player Safety.’’ ”That’s their job,’’ Maurice said. Well, it was not done. Wilson knew full well that Vilmanis was in a vulnerable position along the boards. Vilmanis worked the puck up the ice and Wilson bulldozed him from behind, planting the Florida forward face-first into the dasher boards. There was no doubt it was a boarding call — the puck left Vilmanis’ stick moments before impact — and Wilson had full view of Vilmanis’ number, name plate, and even the small Panthers’ logo on the back of his white helmet. Ever see a young hockey player wearing a jersey to a game and notice the big red stop sign stitched onto the back? It there as a reminder to players not to hit another player in the back. When you see the numbers, stop. Perhaps teams playing the Capitals from now on should put those stop signs on the back of their sweaters. Probably would not help anyway. Vilmanis, 22, missed Sunday’s game in Boston and will likely be out tonight in Columbus as well. Maurice said the Panthers will not know the severity of Vilmanis’ injury until team doctors in Florida get to take a look at him. It is possible Vilmanis skipped the team charter and returned to town. Vilmanis is expected to be fine and he will return to the Florida lineup in time. That is not the point. Wilson has been a dangerous and, based on his 30-plus goals the past two seasons, very talented forward in this league who is now making high-end money. He does not need to keep playing this way to “keep his edge” nor to keep his job. Again, he just needs to do better. Perhaps some day. item.title: Stephen Curry's Warriors make NBA history with eight straight wins after 0-3 start
item.description: Stephen Curry's Warriors make NBA history with eight straight wins after 0-3 start originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Golden State Warriors have completed a remarkable turnaround that no NBA team had previously accomplished. After opening the 2026-27 season with three consecutive losses, Golden State has won eight straight games, culminating in Monday's 138-87 demolition of the New Orleans Pelicans . The win improved the Warriors to 8-3 and completed an undefeated five-game homestand. More importantly, it established a historic distinction for a team that looked vulnerable during the opening week. No previous NBA team had followed an 0-3 start with eight consecutive victories. Warriors produce overwhelming performance Golden State controlled Monday's game almost immediately, building a 35-20 lead after the first quarter. EIGHT IN A ROW SOUNDS FANTASTIC 😎 https://t.co/G3jPIVyOtc — Golden State Warriors (@warriors) November 10, 2026 The Warriors extended their advantage to 72-43 by halftime and never allowed New Orleans to mount a serious comeback. Brandin Podziemski and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg each scored 25 points, while Curry added 25 points in fewer than 21 minutes. Lendeborg shot 8-for-10 from the field and contributed seven rebounds and four assists, demonstrating the depth that has supported Golden State's recent success. Twelve of the 13 Warriors who appeared in the game scored, highlighting an offensive performance that extended far beyond the team's biggest star. Curry remains central to the turnaround Curry entered Monday averaging 31.3 points per game, ranking second in the NBA. The 38-year-old had scored 41 points during Saturday's overtime victory over Orlando, providing another reminder of his ability to dominate games well into the later stages of his career. Golden State's winning streak has featured contributions from several players, but Curry's shooting and offensive gravity remain fundamental to the team's identity. Opposing defenses must account for him throughout each possession, creating opportunities for teammates to attack favorable situations. MORE : Celtics receive alarming Paul George warning as NBA scout suggests 60-game limit Golden State now faces a different challenge The Warriors have recovered from an 0-3 start, but their next test involves sustaining that momentum away from home. Golden State begins a five-game road trip Wednesday against the Houston Rockets . The team will also monitor the status of reserve guard Brandon Williams, who left Monday's game with a left hamstring injury and is scheduled for further evaluation. Eight straight wins have transformed the Warriors' early-season outlook. For Curry and his teammates, the challenge is now proving that the turnaround can continue when the schedule becomes less favorable. item.title: FIA reveals latest ADUO results in final review of 2026 F1 season
item.description: Motorsport photo The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers. From this season, the FIA installed a mechanism in the F1 regulations which allowed power unit manufacturers the ability to make updates, if they fell behind the leading engine, in the form of tokens permitted under a performance scale. After the first period in 2026, which ran from the Australian Grand Prix to the Canadian GP, it was announced that Red Bull Ford Powertrains emerged as the benchmark, while Mercedes ’ internal combustion engine trails by between 2-4%, which gave the German manufacturer to one additional upgrade this year and one more next season. Ferrari , Audi and Honda fell into the category of being more than 4% behind on ICE power, which grants them two upgrades during the current campaign and two more in 2027. Red Bull Ford Powertrains asked for a review of the ADUO analysis, which delayed the official publication of the first results, as it disputed the results and being considered the manufacturer with the strongest engine. As agreed before the start of the season by the teams, the FIA only measures the internal combustion engine, but once a manufacturer qualifies for ADUO, it is also allowed to modify electrical components such as the battery and MGU-K. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing So while Red Bull’s rivals have been able to install power unit upgrades across this season, the Milton Keynes-based effort has effectively faced an engine freeze. In the third and final FIA analysis of ADUO – which took engine data from the Dutch GP up to and including the US GP – there has been no change and therefore no manufacturer will gain or lose its current concessions. There was also no change in the second ADUO period over the summer. “For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers,” an FIA report stated. Given the dispute over how ADUO is measured, the FIA is open to changes in the system in the future, subject to approval from the power unit manufacturers, while FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis is confident the concept is working as desired. “The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” Tombazis said. Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Nikolas Tombazis, FIA “The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1. “However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose. To that end, we have been working closely with the power unit manufacturers and team

item.title: Kenan Yildiz reveals comeback date as Juventus star prepares to end four month injury nightmare
item.description: Galatasaray-vs-Juventus-Champions-League-2025-26-KO-play-offs-1s - AFP Kenan Yildiz is nearing his highly anticipated return for Juventus after missing several months of action due to injury. The talented forward recently provided a positive update on his recovery, revealing his target date to finally step back onto the pitch this December. Juventus handed major injury boost Yildiz is finally closing in on a return to action for Juventus following a frustrating spell on the sidelines. The 21-year-old has been unavailable due to injury since August , dealing a significant blow to the Italian club. According to Tuttosport , the talented forward will soon resume his individual training programme at the Continassa base. He will then gradually increase his physical workload as he builds up his crucial match fitness. Yildiz will not be ready to feature immediately after the current international break. Juventus are carefully managing his recovery process to ensure he returns in optimal physical condition. Yildiz reveals his comeback timeline The attacker recently attended a ceremony in Bologna on Monday to collect the Bulgarelli Number 8 award. During the event, he provided a highly positive update regarding his ongoing rehabilitation. Yildiz confirmed directly to those in attendance that he expects to be back "in December". The Juventus number 10 expressed his deep desire to get back onto the pitch and contribute alongside his team-mates. "I feel good and I hope to be playing again soon," Yildiz explained when discussing his fitness. "I miss Juventus so much. I miss the feeling of playing football." Coping without the number ten Juventus have been forced to navigate the early months of the campaign without their creative focal point. Despite the lengthy and frustrating absence, Luciano Spalletti has notably refused to use the injury as an excuse. The club and medical staff have now plotted a clear timeline for his gradual reintroduction. A return against Monza on Monday, 14 December at the Allianz Stadium is currently viewed as the most realistic target. Yildiz remains eager to accelerate that process if his body allows it over the next fortnight. The coaching staff will monitor his daily progress closely as he ramps up his training workload. Crucial fixtures await the forward While the Monza fixture remains the primary objective, Juventus are quietly hoping Yildiz could make the matchday squad even sooner. His early availability would provide a timely lift for the busy winter schedule. An accelerated recovery could see him feature in the domestic home game against Udinese on 6 December. Alternatively, he might travel for the Europa League clash against Hapoel Be’er Sheva in Bucharest just four days later. A December return will ultimately provide a massive mid-season boost for Juventus. Yildiz will now focus entirely on completing his individual work at Continassa to make that comeback a reality.

item.title: ‘Don’t do that’ – JuJu Watkins shuts down announcer over Caitlin Clark diss
item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Minutes after dropping 51 points, Juju Watkins was standing on business with the game announcer. Dropping 51 points in a single game put JuJu Watkins in a rare group, but it’s how she’s bounced back from last year’s injury setback that really tells you who she is. Any fear that missing time would mess with her rhythm got erased fast, as she’s been absolutely unguardable this season. It feels like everyone already knows where this is heading. WNBA teams are practically counting down the days until she’s draft-eligible, and she looks every bit ready for the pro game right now. Juju Watkins defends Caitlin Clark JuJu Watkins wasn’t letting anyone pit her against greatness. Right after setting the season’s scoring high, an announcer tried enticing her with a cheap “ Caitlin Clark who?” comment, but Watkins shut it down before he could even finish: “No, don’t do that. Don’t do that. Much respect, Eric.” Announcer said: “There’s a lot of players in the country playing Division 1 basketball. Nobody scored more points in one game this year than you. That’s the most. Caitlin Clark who?” Juju Watkins replied: “No, no, no. Don’t do that. Don’t do that. Don’t do that. Much respect, Eric.” It feels like commentators physically cannot talk about women’s basketball without dragging Caitlin Clark into it. Dropping her name for cheap engagement steals the spotlight from whatever night Watkins just had, stirring up fake drama out of nowhere instead of just giving flowers where they’re due. item.title: Big Ten Tournament semifinal preview: No. 5-seed Maryland men’s soccer vs. No. 1-seed Indiana
item.description: The University of Maryland Men’s Soccer team ended in a tie game against UCLA at Ludwig Field on September 25th 2026. | Photo by Jessie Reider/Testudo Times Following No. 5-seed Maryland men’s soccer’s convincing 2-1 victory over No. 4-seed Michigan State, the Terps will now face top-seed Indiana on the road for the second time this season. Maryland has struggled in away games this season, owning a 3-3 record in those games. The Hoosiers haven’t lost at home since Nov. 3, 2025. The game will begin at 6 p.m. in Bloomington, Indiana, and will be televised on Big Ten Network. The winner of the match will play the winner of No. 3-seed Rutgers and No. 2-seed Washington for the Big Ten championship. The highest seed in the final will host the championship game. What happened last time The last matchup between the two Big Ten soccer powerhouses was a top-10 matchup with the then-No. 6 Terps and the then-No. 2 Hoosiers. Maryland stumbled out the gate in Big Ten play, totaling four points in the three games entering the match, while Indiana had an immaculate 3-0-1 conference record. Head coach Todd Yeagley’s squad showed it was the superior team in a dominant 3-1 Hoosiers victory. Indiana controlled the game from the kickoff with smart passes and a suffocating press. Its first goal came in the 17th minute from a Maryland own goal, when Kenny Quist-Therson’s clearance deflected off Leon Koehl into Maryland’s net. Two minutes later, the Hoosiers extended their lead with a Charlie Heuer goal. Former Terp Stephane Njike sparked the run that led to the goal and later found the net himself in the 63rd minute after two stellar saves from Laurin Mack. Rodrigo Neri netted the Terps’ lone goal in the 71st minute, but Michal Mroz — the Big Ten leader in save percentage, shutouts and the fewest goals against — silenced Maryland for the remainder of the game. Maryland head coach Sasho Cirovski left the match with frustrations and questions about the Terps’ defensive execution and cohesion along the backline. What’s happened since Indiana has continued its dominance since the October bout, finishing No. 5 in RPI and boasting a 14-1-3 record while winning the Big Ten regular season title. Over that time, they also captured ranked wins against No. 16 Michigan State and No. 25 UCLA. Oliver Moller-Jenson finished as the Hoosiers leading scorer with 12 goals during the regular season, which is good for eighth nationally. Mroz also finished the year as one of the nation’s top goalkeepers with top-five finishes in save percentage and goals against average. The Terps’ defense has improved mightily since the Indiana game, getting three shutouts in its last five games. They also allowed just one goal to Michigan State in their win and exhibited refined defense against set pieces. Three things to watch 1. Rest or momentum? item.title: US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The United States House of Representatives is set to hold a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s efforts to protect Christians and tackle insecurity in the Middle Belt, with Republican lawmaker Chris Smith leading the session on Thursday, November 12. According to a statement issued by Smith’s office on Monday, the session is titled ‘One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria’s Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt’, with hearing scheduled for 11am at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington, DC. It partly reads, “Congressional hearing that assesses the current state of religious violence perpetrated by radical Islamists, such as Boko Haram and Fulani terrorists, against Christians in Nigeria; the Nigerian government’s efforts to curb the persecution and punish those responsible for committing atrocities against Christian and non-radical Muslim communities; and the steps the United States can take to ensure that Nigerian officials are addressing and preventing the systemic violence against Christians and non-radical Muslims by Islamist extremists.” The first panel will feature Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, and Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour. The second panel will include Nina Shea, senior fellow and director of the Centre for Religious Freedom at the Hudson Institute; Ryan Brown, chief executive officer of Open Doors US; and Oge Onubogu, director and senior fellow of the Africa Programme at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. The hearing will be streamed live on YouTube. This will be Smith’s 14th congressional hearing exclusively on Nigeria. In November 2025, he chaired a hearing after President Donald Trump’s redesignation of Nigeria as a ‘country of particular concern’. In May 2016, he also chaired a hearing on “The U.S. role in helping Nigeria confront Boko Haram and other threats in northern Nigeria.” The post US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Barcelona defender Cubarsi named 2026 Golden Boy winner
item.description: Barcelona defender Cubarsi named 2026 Golden Boy winner Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsí has won the 2026 Golden Boy award, given to the best Under-21 men’s player in the world. The 19-year-old succeeds Paris Saint-Germain forward Désiré Doué and becomes the fourth Barcelona player to win the prize in the last six years. Cubarsí follows in the footsteps of team-mates Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal, who have all previously claimed the award. He is also the first defender to win the Golden Boy since Matthijs de Ligt, then of Ajax, was named the winner in 2018. The award was established by Italian sports newspaper Tuttosport in 2003 and has previously been won by some of the biggest names in world football. Erling Haaland, Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi are among the former recipients of the prize.

item.title: Why are IPL teams going for all-rounders? Is the end of Impact Player rule a reason behind franchises opting for all-rounders over specialists
item.description: Why are IPL teams going for all-rounders? Is the end of Impact Player rule a reason behind franchises opting for all-rounders over specialists originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: The only completed four-player swap of this window sent two seamers out and brought two all-rounders in. Hardik Pandya is set to join PBKS, while Sam Curran and Romario Shepherd have all been linked with moves. Reports suggest the Impact Player rule could be scrapped after IPL 2027 season. Why are IPL teams going for all-rounders in this trade window? Chennai Super Kings made the most interesting move of this window when they sent Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis, two specialist seamers, to Sunrisers Hyderabad, and took all-rounders Liam Livingstone and Jack Edwards in exchange. The most talked-about move of the IPL 2027 trade window also involves an all-rounder, as India star Hardik Pandya is set to join Punjab Kings. Both MI and Punjab are set to confirm that Pandya left Mumbai on Tuesday, while Arshdeep came the other way. Defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Rajasthan Royals have also been discussing a Romario Shepherd-for-Sam Curran swap, which is a like-for-like trade. Set against the three seasons that preceded it, there is clearly a reverse trend. Since 2023, squads have been built around specialists because of the Impact Player rule, which allowed teams to add an extra player in between matches. MORE: Hardik Pandya-Arshdeep Singh trade: What do MI and PBKS stand to gain from the deal Will the IPL Impact player rule be scrapped? The future of the Impact player rule has been under review since the conclusion of the IPL 2026 campaign. The BCCI wrote to all ten franchises seeking formal feedback before the August 31 deadline, and the subject came up again at the IPL Governing Council meeting , with chairman Arun Dhumal saying only that the matter was under discussion and a call would follow after consulting stakeholders. Sachin Tendulkar urged the board to drop it. Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Hardik Pandya, Axar Patel and Shubman Gill have all raised the same objection: that the rule devalues genuine all-rounders by letting teams field a specialist for every job. The board's own behaviour has been contradictory. In late September 2024, it confirmed the Impact Player would run through the 2025-2027 cycle. Two weeks later, it scrapped the rule from the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, the competition that was used to trial it in the first place. The latest indications are that the rule will stay for the IPL 2027 campaign, however, it could be scrapped before IPL 2028 and its mega-auction. MORE: 'Duniya Hila Denge Hum': Axar Patel trades cheeky banter with Arshdeep Singh amid Hardik Pandya PBKS-MI trade buzz Is the end of the Impact Player rule a reason behind franchises opting for all-rounders over specialists While there is no confirmation on scrapping the Impact Player rule after IPL 2027

item.title: Mancini’s former teammate reveals: ‘He was unbearable at first, I locked him in a room’
item.description: Mancini’s former teammate reveals: ‘He was unbearable at first, I locked him in a room’ Italy coach Roberto Mancini was “unbearable” when they first played together, according to Michele Serena, who says he once locked the Sampdoria star in a room until they sorted out their differences. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, via CalcioMercato , the former full-back looked back on a career that took him from Venezia to Juventus, Sampdoria, Fiorentina, Atlético Madrid, Parma and finally Inter, the club he supported as a boy. He joined Sampdoria from Juventus as part of the deal that took Gianluca Vialli to Turin. “Roberto Mancini? Very good, but unbearable,” Serena said. “I argued with him in my first year, and Mantovani fined him and took my side. Vierchowod told me to apologise to Mancini, so after one training session I locked him in a small room with me until we finally sorted things out. After that, we built a good relationship, and we still speak today.” BURSA, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 28: Roberto Mancini, Head Coach of Italy, looks on before the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Türkiye and Italy at Atatürk Spor Kompleksi Matli Stadyumu on September 28, 2026 in Bursa, Turkey. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) Serena on Mancini, Mihajlović and Batistuta Sinisa Mihajlović was another Sampdoria teammate, and he used to make Serena go in goal. “After training, Mihajlović would put me in goal and take free-kicks. It would finish 20-0 or 20-1 to him.” At Fiorentina, Serena played alongside Gabriel Batistuta and Rui Costa. “Bati was the most complete No 9 I’ve ever seen. With Rui, we always wondered how he could smoke so many cigarettes and then run like that on the pitch. “Edmundo? I’ll never forgive him for not coming back from the Rio Carnival. We had Batistuta out, and we were fighting for the Scudetto.” 12 Sep 1998: Gabriel Batistuta of Fiorentina celebrates during the Serie A match against Empoli at the Stadio Communale in Florence, Italy. Mandatory Credit: Allsport UK /Allsport Serena finished his career at Inter in 2003, but he’s still haunted by 5 May 2002. On the final day of that season, Héctor Cúper’s side lost 4-2 at Lazio, and Juventus took the title. “I wanted to retire by winning the Scudetto with Inter, the team I’ve supported since I was a child. Instead, on that 5 May, I don’t know what happened… It’s a wound that’s still open, and it still hurts too much today. “I was supposed to play that day instead of Gresko. I’d done everything to recover from an injury, but Cúper changed his mind at the last minute. I confronted him about it, because not playing that day really hurt me.”

item.title: “No, They Do Not Miss Him” – Skip Bayless Takes a Shot at LeBron James After Lakers Cruise to NBA Best 10-2 Record
item.description: Luka Doncic, LeBron James - Image © Imagn Images LeBron James keeps catching Skip Bayless’ strays. The veteran analyst got a golden opportunity after the Los Angeles Lakers surged to the top of both conferences on Monday with their sixth straight win. Los Angeles beat the Atlanta Hawks 124-114 on the second night of a back-to-back on the road, despite missing Austin Reaves. Bayless took to X to acknowledge the Lakers’ standing and claimed they don’t miss James. “The Los Angeles Lakers now have the NBA’s best record. No, they do not miss him.” LeBron James shockingly left the Lakers in the 2026 offseason to join the Philadelphia 76ers. The Lakers used their cap space efficiently after his $52.6 million salary came off their books. They improved their core by signing Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Collin Sexton, Ziaire Williams, and Matisse Thybulle in free agency. However, many analysts and fans weren’t confident that the Lakers would win without James, who spent eight seasons in Los Angeles. Skip Bayless seemingly called out those takes with his latest shot at James. Doncic and James’ skills overlapped. They also played similar defensive roles, which impacted the Lakers’ on-court balance. However, with James gone, the Lakers have players in defined roles, especially Doncic, who has been on a tear, averaging 39.3 points, 7.8 rebounds, 7.9 assists, and 2.0 steals, shooting 49.8% from the field and 40.7% from 3. LeBron James’ Sixers were tied for the best record with the Lakers before Monday LeBron James and the Lakers’ breakup may have been the best outcome for both entities. Three weeks into the season, James’ Sixers and the Lakers were tied for the best record (9-2) before Los Angeles got its 10th win on Monday. While the Lakers have looked more surgical on offense, boasting a league-best 121.5 offensive rating, the Sixers have made their mark on defense with a 107.6 rating. The offense hasn’t strung together a series of good runs as its All-Star quartet – James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, and Joel Embiid – figures out its chemistry. Nevertheless, with James in the lineup, Philly is doing just enough to stay afloat offensively. He’s primarily playing as a playmaker, averaging a team-high 6.7 assists. It’s the role he thrives in, and exactly what the Sixers needed. After the Lakers acquired Luka Doncic, LeBron James was no longer playing that role consistently, putting him in an unfamiliar position. Nevertheless, he’s getting opportunities to be a floor general again and seems more comfortable despite playing alongside multiple All-Stars. item.title: “I can’t believe this is happening”, says Brazil newcomer Allan
item.description: “I can’t believe this is happening”, says Brazil newcomer Allan New call-up Allan gave his first press conference with the Brazilian national team on Tuesday (10) and emphasized how hard it still is to believe he has been called up to the Seleção. In Singapore for friendlies against Japan and the hosts, the forward explained that his first few days with the team still do not feel real. “I'm definitely very emotional. I open my phone and, with every message from my father, I get more eager for things to happen. I talk in the family group chat and with my wife about how I can hardly believe what I'm experiencing. Until very recently, this seemed so far away,” he admitted. Allan during his first press conference with the Brazilian national team in Singapore Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF This is his first opportunity with the senior national team. At youth level, he represented the Under-15s while playing for Figueirense. He attended a training camp at Granja Comary in July 2018 and another in Chile in August 2019, when Brazil beat the hosts in two friendlies: 5–0 and 2–1. Despite his nerves, he relies on his family's faith in him to keep his emotions in check and maintain the performances that earned him his call-up. “It's very difficult to come here and see players like Raphinha, Vini Jr. and even Endrick. Being here for the first time... My father tells me I'm capable, that if I'm here, I have talent too. On the pitch, I forget everything and focus fully on my performance,” he stressed. Allan during his first press conference with the Brazilian national team in Singapore Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF Allan, 22, has been playing for England's Manchester City since the middle of the year. Before that, he made his name at Palmeiras, where he played almost a hundred matches and established himself as yet another outstanding talent to emerge from the club. The Florianópolis native, from the state of Santa Catarina, is one of 25 players called up for the friendlies against Japan and Singapore. Brazil face Japan on Saturday (14) at 7:15 a.m. (Brasília time), and the hosts on Tuesday (17) at 7 a.m. (Brasília time). Both matches will take place at Singapore's National Stadium, in a city where Allan is already making fond memories. "Singapore will always have a place in my mind and in my heart. I hope to do well here, in training and in the match," he said. Allan, wearing the number 11 shirt, before a friendly against Chile with Brazil's Under-15 team in August 2019 Credits: Carlos Parra/Comunicaciones ANFP This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Coutinho 2.0? Liverpool make their move for Brazilian starlet after recent contract decision
item.description: Coutinho 2.0? Liverpool make their move for Brazilian starlet after recent contract decision Almost 14 years on from signing Philippe Coutinho , Liverpool are reportedly making moves to potentially sign another Brazilian playmaker who’s been attracting some high-profile European interest. The Reds’ former number 10 spent five years at Anfield, during which time he scored 54 goals in 201 appearances and was a hugely influential figure on the pitch, frequently conjuring up moments of majesty. He was sold in January 2018 and wasn’t around for the peak years of the Jurgen Klopp reign, although there’s an up-and-coming talent from Brazil who LFC will be hoping can become synonymous with a successful era under Andoni Iraola. Liverpool enquire about Erick Bele According to Sport Witness , Liverpool have made official enquiries with Palmeiras about 19-year-old attacking midfielder Erick Bele, with the Brazilian club prepared to start negotiations at €30m (£25m). Paris Saint-Germain have also been in contact regarding the teenager, who signed a contract extension to 2031 with his current employers last week. The youngster stood out during a recent training camp for Brazil under-20s in which he provided three assists across wins over Denmark, United States and Mexico. Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Could Bele go on to become Coutinho 2.0 at Liverpool? Bele has an impressive record at youth level for Palmeiras, with 20 goals in 45 games for their under-20 side, although his development is being managed carefully as he’s made just seven senior appearances so far ( Transfermarkt ). He plays mostly as a number 10 but can also be deployed on the right flank, similar to Harvey Elliott, and it attests to how highly his club value him that they’ve rewarded him with such a lengthy new contract. An analysis from Future Ballers cites finishing, pace, dribbling, technique, heading, off-the-ball movement and creativity among his strongest attributes, marking him out as a well-rounded young talent who also boasts plenty of physical strength. Even if Liverpool were to sign Bele in 2027, realistically he wouldn’t be challenging for a first-team place straight away, given his inexperience at senior level and the presence of Florian Wirtz in the Reds’ XI. A loan move or two to clubs in mainland Europe would likely be arranged in order to enhance his development, but we can certainly see why Anfield chiefs have enquired about an exciting prospect who, in time, could have strong echoes of Coutinho.

item.title: ‘He’s Ready To Go,’ ‘Literally The Call He’s Waiting On’ — Rams Urged To Target Former Texans All-Pro as Puka Nacua Fill-In
item.description: Oct 25, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua (12) runs off the field against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first half at Allegiant Stadium. © David Brytus-Imagn Images DeAndre Hopkins has spent this fall coaching receivers at Georgia Tech, but ESPN analyst Max Browne said Monday that the 34-year-old “works out to stay ready” in case an NFL team calls. The same day, Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay revealed that Puka Nacua has MCL and PCL sprains and turf toe. Nacua caught 14 passes for a season-high 150 yards in Sunday’s 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders before taking a hit to his right knee on the team’s final offensive play. Rams Urged To Target DeAndre Hopkins as Puka Nacua’s Replacement Talking to “The Athletic LIVE,” Browne traced his pitch back to a conversation over the weekend. “I kid you not, on Saturday I was calling the Georgia Tech game, and their assistant receivers coach is DeAndre Hopkins. I was chatting with him on the field.” Hopkins began the season as an assistant on head coach Brent Key’s staff, and a losing fall reshuffled it Monday. Key fired four assistants, including receivers coach Jafar Williams, after Georgia Tech fell to 2-7 overall and 1-5 in the ACC with a fourth straight conference loss. Browne noted what that meant for Hopkins. “He just got elevated to receivers coach today because Georgia Tech had some firings.” The promotion gives Hopkins a bigger role for Georgia Tech’s final three games. Browne, though, thinks an NFL team should be the one calling Hopkins next: “Give D-Hop a call. He’s ready to go.” In the same breath, Browne was careful not to oversell what a team would be getting. “I’m not saying he’s the D-Hop he was six years ago, but that’s literally the type of team and call he’s waiting on.” Hopkins’ 13th and most recent NFL season came with the Baltimore Ravens in 2025, when he caught 22 passes for 330 yards and two touchdowns on 39 targets. He described the kind of opportunity he wanted in a June radio interview, before Georgia Tech hired him in July, saying, “I would love to play for a competitor if that time came.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Meanwhile, McVay gave no firm return date Monday but put a floor on Nacua’s absence. “It’s a strong chance that we put him on IR. So we’re thinking it’s going to be at least a month.” McVay also second-guessed the play call that ended Nacua’s day. “I’d be lying to you if I said I haven’t questioned the decision-making on that last play over and over in my head … it’s stuff that I feel tremendous responsibility for.” That timeline would keep Nacua out of Sunday’s trip to face the Arizona Cardinals and, after the Week 11 bye, home games against the Green Bay Packers on Nov. 25 and the Kansas City Chiefs on Dec. 3. item.title: “Not Moved” – NBA World Scoffs at Lakers’ Six-Game Winning Streak and Forthcoming Games Citing Schedule Strength
item.description: Luka Doncic against the Portland Trail Blazers © @Lakers/X The LA Lakers are among the NBA’s hottest teams, with a six-game winning streak that has propelled them to a Western Conference-leading 10-2 record. The Lakers’ latest win came on Monday, when they beat the Atlanta Hawks 124-114. After the Lakers’ 10-point win over the Hawks, the X account NBACentral tweeted a picture of the team’s next six games, all against teams below .500. Fans scoffed at the Lakers’ upcoming opponents and their current streak. “We are not moved by this schedule,” one fan tweeted . Over the next six days, the Lakers will be visiting the Milwaukee Bucks and the Phoenix Suns. Together, the two teams have won four games in the first two weeks of the NBA season. After that, the purple-and-gold squad faces a nationally televised game against the Charlotte Hornets, two meetings with the Utah Jazz, and a matchup against the Sacramento Kings. In all likelihood, the Lakers will enter each of these games as the favorite. For some fans, though, beating these teams in the bottom half of their conferences isn’t impressive at all. “It Was Important for Me to Grab It”: Luka Doncic Shares Thoughts on Handing Game Ball to Lakers Rookie Cameron Carr During the Lakers-Hawks game on Monday, Luka Doncic stole the ball and pitched it to Cameron Carr. The former Baylor standout threw down a transition dunk to score his first points in his NBA career. After the game, Doncic secured the game ball and handed it to Carr. The six-time NBA All-Star went on to explain the gesture’s significance as he spoke with reporters. “You always want to remember your first bucket. You want to get that ball, so it was important for me to grab it.” In seven minutes of play on Monday, Carr finished with two points and three rebounds. Doncic, meanwhile, had 32 points, eight boards, and 10 assists. item.title: How Ryan Seacrest is giving his old high school football team something it never had
item.description: The future of Dunwoody (GA) High School football is being built by more than just the players on the field. It's being built by hundreds of community members who have come together to give the Wildcats something they've never had before: a stadium of its own. Fueled by a donation from Dunwoody alum and television host Ryan Seacrest and a community-wide fundraising effort, Seacrest Stadium is officially set to break ground the week of Nov. 23, following county approval on Nov. 9. And when it opens next fall, the whole community will be able to call it their own. “I think we’re all kind of part owners of this,” said Steve Fortenberry, former teacher and president of the Dunwoody High School Community Association. “I think you’re really going to see that it wasn’t just the county building this and we show up. This is Dunwoody’s stadium. We are kind of the Green Bay Packers of the high schools.” The project has been years in the making, but it took a collective effort from the community to turn the vision into a reality. It started with a donation of more than $1 million from Seacrest, who played defensive back for the Wildcats before graduating in 1993. “For us, it’s about so much more than a field,” Seacrest said in a statement provided to USA TODAY Sports. “It’s about creating a place where kids can dream big, chase those dreams and have the support of their families every step of the way. “To be part of something that celebrates both the dreams and the people who help make them possible is what makes this moment so special.” Seacrest’s donation made what once seemed like an unrealistic goal attainable, giving the community a foundation to launch its own fundraising effort: the “Bring It Home Dunwoody” campaign. In October, the school officially reached its goal of raising an additional $1.5 million. The money, raised by nearly 800 community members, will go towards 2,000 new stadium seats, a press box, restrooms, concessions and other stadium amenities. “There is something special about our community that you have to be a part of it to really understand how special Wildcat Pride is and what Dunwoody is all about," said Tom Bass, principal of Dunwoody High School. For years, however, Dunwoody hasn't had a place to call home. In 2020, Dunwoody added a turf field and 1,000 bleacher seats. But hosting home varsity football games requires a minimum seating capacity of 3,000. Instead, schools throughout the Dekalb County School District share stadiums, leaving Dunwoody’s football team with roughly a 15-minute drive to play its home games. “Every game is kind of like a road game for preparing,” said junior tight end Charlie Survilas. “We don’t have the luxury of having our pregame here, playing here – the timing is different, so we have to take the bus to everything.” As a public school system, the Dekalb County School District has other priorities that take precedence over athletic facilities. “We have $2 billion of deferred maintenance in the entire s

item.title: Arizona high school football playoffs: 7 underrated players to watch in the Open Division
item.description: The brackets are set for the Arizona high school football playoffs , and the Open Division will be one of the most competitive series in the country. Of the 12 teams competing in the state's top division, three have been in the Super 25 national rankings at some point in the season, a fourth is currently on the cusp of entering and a fifth has seen time in the Super 15 West Region rankings. Others are jockeying for position to prove they deserve the chance to fight for the top spot in Arizona. More: Arizona high school football player delivers unforgettable national anthem performance While major Division I recruits tend to garner a majority of the headlines, some of the biggest difference-makers will be players whose rising prominence locally is not reflected at the national level. Every state has players like this. The highlight packages look good, the statistics stand out, but for whatever reason, they haven’t distinguished themselves among peers as collegiate recruits. Universities simply aren’t buying in. Oftentimes it’s due to size, pointed out by Chandler (AZ) head coach Ty Wisdom. “It sucks because you know that kid can play,” he told USA TODAY Sports. “You can’t measure their heart.” Below are seven seniors who have been undervalued in the recruiting space and game-changers who have a final shot to showcase what has made them among Arizona's best high school football players. Strong performances may lead to more offers, but as Wisdom says, the shift of the college landscape and transfer portal has taken away excuses. “The great thing about college football now is they can be at a smaller level and they go dominate,” he said. “The days of being like, ‘Oh I’m being overlooked…’ OK, go be overlooked and then show out at Division II, and then you’re going to get moved up.” Marc Duerson III, LB, Basha (Chandler, AZ) College: Northern Arizona University Basha linebacker Marc Duerson has 94 tackles, six tackles for loss, two passes defended, three forced fumbles in a single game, and a sack — yet no stars and just two college offers. Committed to Northern Arizona University, he has been big for the Bears' highly touted defense, helping the team remain among the best in Arizona. He’s aggressive and powerful at the point of attack, and there’s a reason the Arizona Republic ranked him as the top defensive player in Arizona earlier in the season. Duerson was also voted USA TODAY Sports Super 25 Playmaker of the Week in early September. The Bears are reigning back-to-back champions, and the team's high-powered defense will give them a shot to make it three in a row. Duerson's performance at linebacker will be pivotal against other top competition.
